content.summary_of_the_paper: The paper proposes an encoder-decoder-based approach along with instance-feature transformation toward data augmentation in few-shot learning. Some additional tricks (e.g., prototype rectification and compactness constraint) are being proposed to further improve the performance.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
There are plenty of previous works that propose encoder-decoder-based data augmentation [1, 2, 3, 4]. Despite these works being cited, the authors have not clearly explained the differentiation between the proposed STDA versus these methods. Superior performance does not imply the proposed method is significantly distinctive, given that few-show learning has a high deviation in the performance, any minor differences in hyperparameter choice can result in drastic quantitative differences (e.g., the authors directly copy the TriNet performance from its performance from the original paper, it is even worse than the ProtoNet baseline). A carefully conducted ablation under the same code base (instead of copy-and-paste quantitative values from previous papers, unless the authors use the exact same codebase) is required, and more analyses are needed for further understanding of how the proposed algorithm is distinctive compared to its predecessors.

[2] "Delta-encoder: an effective sample synthesis method for few-shot object recognition."
[3] "Free lunch for few-shot learning: Distribution calibration."

content.confidence: 5: You are absolutely certain about your assessment. You are very familiar with the related work and checked the math/other details carefully.
content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper aims to generate features for novel classes which can be used directly with a classifier to perform few-shot classification. Features are generated by first finding their neighbor base classes and then transforming the semantic representation of the examples coming from that base classes to novel classes and finally transforming those semantic representations back to the visual representations.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strengths: 
- Transformations from visual-to-semantic-to-visual are performed by tied weights [1] which makes the whole process efficient.
- Detailed experimental analysis.
- Paper is easy to understand, framework is explained well.

Weaknesses: 
- SOTA tables should have been separated in a similar way to [2,3] to distinguish the models where the semantic side information is used and is not used.
- When making comparisons with different approaches it is important to have the same backbone architecture. In addition, depending on how the feature extractor is trained (e.g, pretrained with base classes + end-to-end vs only end-to-end) there can be significant performance difference simply due to the backbone. This is especially important since few-shot-learning greatly benefits from good feature representations [3].
- The writing can be improved “... To ensure generate semantically meaningful …”
- Eq. 14 looks to be out of place and likely to be before section 3.3.
- Version of GloVe embeddings seems unclear.

[1] Elyor Kodirov, Tao Xiang, and Shaogang Gong. Semantic autoencoder for zero-shot learning.

[2] Chen Xing, Negar Rostamzadeh, Boris Oreshkin, and Pedro O. Pinheiro. Adaptive cross-modal few-shot learning.

[3] O. B. Baran, R. G. Cinbis. Semantics-driven Attentive Few-shot Learning over Clean and Noisy Samples. arXiv.

[3] Gidaris, Spyros & Bursuc, Andrei & Komodakis, Nikos & Perez, Patrick & Cord, Matthieu. (2019). Boosting Few-Shot Visual Learning With Self-Supervision.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: Paper presents the ideas clearly and supports them with thorough experiments apart from a couple of small issues. Although the idea of generating visual features from semantic space is not novel, the way transformations from visual-to-semantic-to-visual are being done is unique and effective. Paper looks to be easy to reproduce considering the amount of given details for implementation.
content.summary_of_the_review: Although paper lacks novelty, the use of transformations with tied weights and the way of training the encoder, decoder and semantic transformation module are interesting parts of the paper. Apart from some relatively minor categorization issues in SOTA tables, experimental results are overall satisfactory to justify the effectiveness of the model. My preliminary evaluation is inclined towards acceptance.

content.confidence: 4: You are confident in your assessment, but not absolutely certain. It is unlikely, but not impossible, that you did not understand some parts of the submission or that you are unfamiliar with some pieces of related work.
content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper proposes a data augmentation framework based on semantic feature transformation. The proposed method STDA transfers samples from the base dataset to the novel task in an encoder-decoder paradigm based on the semantic transformation between similar base and novel classes. Moreover, it introduces a prototype rectification approach by combining the features of the support set and query set to reduce prototype bias. Exhaustive ablation studies and comparison experiments show the method outperforms the state-of-the-arts.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength:
● The paper is well written and easy to follow while insights are conveyed in a logical way. 
● The experiments are well-studied and the results are appealing, validating the effectiveness of the proposed framework.
Weakness:
● Lack of novelty. Data augmentation in a hidden space (semantic space in this paper) and the framework of "encoder-data transformation-decoder" have been a baseline data augmentation approach these years, e.g., "DeVries T, Taylor G W. Dataset augmentation in feature space. arXiv preprint arXiv:1702.05538, 2017." Additionally, the idea of incorporating the features of the query set to rectify the prototype is not novel, e.g., "Liu J, Song L, Qin Y. Prototype rectification for few-shot learning[C]//European Conference on Computer Vision. Springer, Cham, 2020: 741-756.". Please highlight the contribution of the paper to clarify the novelty.
● Lack of references. As declared in the paper, the proposed method made a contribution to prototype rectification. It is essential to compare the previous methods of prototype rectification/optimization. The introduction of the related works is suggested to be included in the corresponding section and also the experimental comparison is supposed to be completed. Please add the following references and especially clarify the difference between the proposed method and [1]:
[1] Liu J, Song L, Qin Y. Prototype rectification for few-shot learning[C]//European Conference on Computer Vision. Springer, Cham, 2020: 741-756.
[2] Zhang B, Li X, Feng S, et al. MetaNODE: Prototype optimization as a neural ODE for few-shot learning[C]//Proceedings of the AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence. 2022, 36(8): 9014-9021.
● Lack of clarity. The novelty of this work mainly lies in data augmentation, which alleviates the data insufficiency problem. However, how to determine the number of augmented features (K' in the paper) to improve the performance? By comparing the experimental results in Table.1, 2, and 5, it is obvious that the results in Table.1 and 2 are obtained by different values of K'. The additional procedure of tuning the best K' apparently increases the complexity of the method. Please clarify the method of tuning K' and declare the values of K' in Table1 and 2 (or show the results with a fixed experimental value of K'). 
● Please complete the experimental results of other methods on all the datasets as long as it is available, e.g., the method ProtoComNet (Zhang et al., 2021a) has shown the experimental result on the CUB dataset but it is not seen in Table. 2.
● Symbol errors. The usage of subscript and superscript of the symbols in Fig. 2 is not consistent with that in formulas.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
Quality: The paper is easy to follow while insights are conveyed in a logical way, but lacks some references.
Clarity: The paper is basically clear, but the important details about hyper-parameter K' are missing or unclear.
Novelty: The paper makes incremental advances over the current state-of-the-art.
Reproducibility: Key resources (e.g., code) are unavailable and some key details (e.g., the procedure of tuning K') are unavailable which makes it difficult to reproduce the main results.
content.summary_of_the_review: The paper is well written and easy to follow and the experiments are well-studied with appealing results. However, the work lacks novelty, clarity of some details, and comparison with the highly related works.
content.correctness: 4: All of the claims and statements are well-supported and correct.
content.technical_novelty_and_significance: 3: The contributions are significant and somewhat new. Aspects of the contributions exist in prior work.
content.empirical_novelty_and_significance: 2: The contributions are only marginally significant or novel.

content.title: Response to the comments
content.comment:
$\underline{ Response:}$
We would like to thank the reviewer for providing valuable critiques and suggestions, which further strengthen our manuscript. We have revised our manuscript based on the comments. All changes are highlighted in blue. A detailed point by point response is provided. We hope our response has fully addressed the comments from reviewer. 

1.

R: Thanks for the comment. Our encoder-decoder paradigm differs from the existing methods in that the augmented features are transformed from similar classes rather than put some perturbations on the latent feature embeddings, which can generate features close to real samples. And the augmentation process is implemented on the semantic space rather than on an arbitrary latent embedding space, which can generate semantically meaningful features. We also impose reconstruction constraints on the encoder and decoder. Parameters of the encoder and decoder are trained with weight tying. While some of the previous works, such as the method proposed in [3], augments samples in an arbitrary feature space, and the features are projected to the latent space without any constraint.

As for the prototype rectification method, BD-CSPN method [1] rectifies the prototypes with pseudo-labeled query samples, which are predicted by comparing the similarity to the basic prototypes (which is biased due to limited samples). Those pseudo-labels cannot be completely correct, which will produce negative impact on the prototype rectification. While our method rectifies the prototypes with the cluster centers of the unlabeled samples. The clustering procedure relies on the data distribution of the unlabeled data, which is agnostic to the support samples. Thus, the cluster centers won’t introduce biased information caused by limited support data. And the cluster centers are assigned labels based on a global optimization strategy, which has never been exploited before.

2.

R: We are sorry for missing some highly related works. As suggested, we have added a detailed discussion about the difference between our method and those related works in the introduction section. And we have also added the experimental results of these methods on table 1 and table 2. All changes are highlighted in blue in the revised manuscript.

3.

R: Thanks for the comment. We determine the optimal K value by a traverse experiment on the validation dataset for each datasets. And it can be observed from figure 3 that different datasets have different optimal K values. As suggested, we record the performance of different datasets on fixed K values. Experiments are implemented in transductive setting.
